newsitem.title: FINLAND: CHANCES EXIST FOR NEXT PAY DEAL LIKE CURRENT - LUNDH.
newsitem.headline: CHANCES EXIST FOR NEXT PAY DEAL LIKE CURRENT - LUNDH.

text.p: There are good chances for a similar incomes settelment to be agreed in autumn 1997 as the current moderate agreement, said Per-Erik Lundh, chairman of the metal workers union.

In an interview with Reuters at the council meeting of the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK), Lundh said this would be possible if the real wage development in the year up to autumn next year is as even between various sectors as it was in the first year of the current settlement.
"I would say that the chances are the best ever, if the trend in wages is that even", he said. But there can be pressures if the development has varied, he said.
The current pay deal increased wages only modestly in the first year.

Lundh also said that although there are some signs of mounting political pressures within the government and even inside the coalition parties, the government still looks strong enough to contribute to the birth of a pay deal much like the current one by offering income tax cuts.
The fact the union plans to decide a final stance on Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) next autumn will have an indirect impact on the wage talks, he said.

He also said that the strongest criticism of EMU on the labour market side was probably seen in the paper sector, not his union, and on the field in general since the grassroots have a clear emotional tie to the markka whereas the benefits of EMU are very abstract.
The paper workers work in an industry which depends heavily on trends in the dollar, he noted.

The metal workers main demands in order to accept EMU are that companies would build up a strong enough balance sheets, that they would be able to create funds to work as buffers against economic fluctuations and that wage systems would be flexible.
Asked whether he shared the SAK's view that Finland should not join EMU if employment fails to improve markedly, he said "I would not be as categorical".
